Uomo di 75 anni. PSA 7,0 ng/mL; volume p: 75-year-old man. PSA 7.0 ng/mL; prostate volume about 23 mL (PSA density about 0.30 ng/mL²). Prostate MRI at 3 T (axial T2, calculated high-b diffusion and ADC map; dynamic sequences not available).
Il valore assoluto del PSA da solo ingan:
The absolute PSA value alone is misleading: 7 ng/mL in a small gland (23 mL) gives a PSA density of about 0.30, which is highly suspicious (threshold 0.15-0.20). In large prostates the same PSA may be due to hypertrophy.
In the peripheral zone the deciding sequence is diffusion: focal area bright at high b and dark on ADC, with marked restriction and a diameter of at least 1.5 cm = PI-RADS 5. T2 serves to define the extent and the relationships with the capsule (bulging, irregularity, obliteration of the rectoprostatic angle, involvement of the neurovascular bundle) and with the seminal vesicles.
In this patient all the cores, systematic and targeted, on both sides were positive for Gleason 4+5: extensive, high-risk disease.
Here the ADC of the lesion is reduced but not very low (about 800-1,000 × 10⁻⁶ mm²/s, measured with a small ROI in the darkest part): the high b is clearly hyperintense. At the borderline between "markedly" and "moderately" hypointense: for this reason 4 and 5 are both defensible, and the decision (biopsy) does not change.
Guarda la densità del PSA, non solo il P: Look at PSA density, not just PSA: 7 ng/mL in 23 mL is highly suspicious.
Biopsia con fusione RM-ecografia: adenoc: MRI-ultrasound fusion biopsy: Gleason 4+5 = 9 (ISUP 5) adenocarcinoma in all right and left systematic cores and in all targeted cores, up to 16 mm of tumor per core (data from the Prostate-MRI-US-Biopsy collection).
